Q: Validate Index for a Collection A:

I don't know how you tested your statement about the various data types being accepted as keys on your MAC since you provide no code, but on the PC it definitely does not work.

I think you need to constrain your keys to be strings. On the PC, here is an example of what happens if you do not:

The code below throws error 457 (already assigned key) when trying to add the 3rd element. The 1 is interpreted as positional but we've already assigned an element in that position.

Option Explicit
Sub due()
    Dim Col As Collection
    Dim a
    Dim v As Variant
    
a = Array("a", "b", 1, 2, 3, "X", "Y", "Z", 40000000#, 21)

Set Col = New Collection
For Each v In a
    Col.Add Item:=v, Key:=v
Next v
Stop
End Sub

This code will throw a type mismatch error when trying to add 40000000# and also note that the quoted smaller numbers in the array are not interpreted as positional. Actually, any numeric value larger than the number of items in the collection will throw a type mismatch error, and a numeric value that has already been used will throw a 457 error

Option Explicit
Sub due()
    Dim Col As Collection
    Dim a
    Dim v As Variant
    
a = Array("a", "b", "1", "2", "3", "X", "Y", "Z", 40000000#, 21)

Set Col = New Collection
For Each v In a
    Col.Add Item:=v, Key:=v
Next v
Stop
End Sub

Q: Why facing "CUDA error: device-side assert triggered" while training LSTM model? A:

The most likely cause: your problem statement says "outputs 1 to 9" but CrossEntropyLoss expects 0-indexed labels [0, num_classes). Index 9 is out of bounds for a 9-class model and triggers the assert silently on GPU.

Check it:

print(labels.min(), labels.max())  # should be 0 and 8, not 1 and 9

Fix:

labels = labels - 1

To get the real error message, run one batch on CPU — the GPU swallows the details:

model.cpu()
outputs = model(text_input.long(), gene_input.long(), variance_input.long())
loss = criterion(outputs, labels)

Also verify your embedding indices don't exceed their vocab sizes — LabelEncoder is 0-indexed so gene_size must equal len(encoder.classes_).

More causes and diagnostics: Fix CUDA error: device-side assert triggered in PyTorch

Q: issues running multiple build jobs in parallel usin DIND A:

When NOT running in kubernetes and using a gitlab runner with multi-concurrency similar to the following:

concurrent = 5

[[runners]]
  executor = "docker"
  environment = ["FF_NETWORK_PER_BUILD=1"]
  [runners.docker]
    image = "docker"

  1. Ensure you've set FF_NETWORK_PER_BUILD as per the above.

  2. In your .gitlab-ci.yml, set the following:

    variables:
  DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker:2375
  DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: ""

Q: SourceTree Error: 'git status' failed with code 128: error: inflate: data stream error (incorrect header check) A:

This worked for me. I reinitialized the repo and fixed my problem.

git init
git add .
git commit -m "Reinitialize repo"
